p2.ex2: A poor diet can damage your long-term health over time.

p2.en: Achieving good results without wasting time or resources.
p2.example: Short, focused workouts can be just as efficient as longer sessions.
p2.ex1: She developed an efficient morning routine that took only thirty minutes.
p2.ex2: Planning meals in advance is an efficient way to maintain a healthy diet.

p2.en: To cause physical or mental damage to someone or something.
p2.example: Skipping rest days can harm your progress rather than help it.
p2.ex1: Unhealthy diets harm both your body and your energy levels.
p2.ex2: She was careful not to harm her joints by choosing low-impact exercises.

p2.en: To become healthy again after an injury or illness.
p2.example: With proper rest and nutrition, most minor injuries heal within a week.
p2.ex1: The wound healed quickly because she kept it clean.
p2.ex2: He gave his muscles time to heal before returning to training.

p2.en: Made from or relating to herbs or plants.
p2.example: She drank herbal tea every evening to help her relax before bed.
p2.ex1: The pharmacist suggested a herbal remedy for his stress headaches.
p2.ex2: Many traditional cultures rely on herbal treatments for minor illnesses.

p2.en: One of the parts or elements that make up a mixture or recipe.
p2.example: The main ingredient in a healthy lifestyle is consistency.
p2.ex1: She checked all the ingredients on the supplement label.
p2.ex2: Fresh ingredients are essential for a nutritious home-cooked meal.

p2.en: To fix equipment or software in a place where it can be used.
p2.example: The city council decided to install outdoor gym equipment in the park.
p2.ex1: She installed a fitness app to track her daily steps.
p2.ex2: He installed a pull-up bar in the doorframe of his home.

p2.en: The way a person lives, including habits, attitudes, and daily choices.
p2.example: Adopting an active lifestyle reduces the risk of many long-term illnesses.
p2.ex1: She made small but significant changes to her lifestyle over six months.
p2.ex2: A sedentary lifestyle increases the risk of heart disease.

p2.en: Relating to or involving a long period of time.
p2.example: The long-term benefits of regular exercise far outweigh the short-term effort.
p2.ex1: She focused on long-term health rather than quick results.
p2.ex2: Long-term habits are built through daily repetition, not willpower alone.

p2.en: To keep something in its current state; to continue doing something regularly.
p2.example: It is harder to maintain good habits than to start them.
p2.ex1: She maintained her fitness level throughout the winter.
p2.ex2: He found it difficult to maintain his diet during the holiday period.

p2.en: The reason or desire that makes you want to do something.
p2.example: Motivation fluctuates, so building discipline is more important than relying on it.
p2.ex1: She found motivation by joining a group fitness class.
p2.ex2: His motivation increased when he started seeing real results.

p2.en: A doctor's written instruction for a medicine or treatment.
p2.example: He needed a prescription for the stronger medication after his injury.
p2.ex1: She picked up her prescription from the pharmacy on the way home.
p2.ex2: Some supplements require a prescription in certain countries.

p2.en: Correct, suitable, or as it should be done.
p2.example: Eating properly and sleeping enough are the foundation of good health.
p2.ex1: He was not stretching properly, which led to a pulled muscle.
p2.ex2: She learned how to warm up properly from a certified trainer.

p2.en: The standard of something; how good or bad it is.
p2.example: The quality of your sleep has a direct impact on your health.
p2.ex1: She focused on the quality of her workouts rather than the quantity.
p2.ex2: Good quality food does not have to be expensive.

p2.en: Relating to or involving only a short period of time.
p2.example: Short-term motivation is useful, but long-term habits are what matter.
p2.ex1: Crash diets may give short-term results but are not sustainable.
p2.ex2: She focused on short-term goals while building towards a larger aim.

p2.en: The outer layer covering the body of a person or animal.
p2.example: Exercise improves circulation, which benefits skin health.
p2.ex1: She applied cream to protect her skin during outdoor training.
p2.ex2: Drinking enough water keeps the skin hydrated and healthy.

p2.en: Contact and communication with other people.
p2.example: Group fitness classes offer great social interaction alongside exercise.
p2.ex1: She valued the social interaction she got from her running club.
p2.ex2: Social interaction is important for mental well-being.

p2.en: Not safe; involving risk of harm.
p2.example: Exercising with an untreated injury is unsafe and can cause further damage.
p2.ex1: She avoided the unsafe path and chose a well-lit route instead.
p2.ex2: It is unsafe to exercise intensely in extreme heat without hydrating.

p2.en: At any time that; every time that something happens.
p2.example: Whenever you feel stressed, try taking a short walk outside.
p2.ex1: She does breathing exercises whenever she feels anxious.
p2.ex2: He puts on his trainers whenever he needs to clear his mind.

p2.en: At a speed that is comfortable for you personally, not following others.
p2.example: She trained at her own pace and avoided comparing herself to others.
p2.ex1: Everyone learns at their own pace — there is no rush.
p2.ex2: He ran at his own pace and finished feeling strong.

p2.en: To have the ability or skill to do something.
p2.example: With the right habits, you are capable of achieving far more than you think.
p2.ex1: She proved she was capable of running a marathon.
p2.ex2: He was not sure he was capable of changing his lifestyle, but he did.

p2.en: To match the speed or rhythm set by someone else.
p2.example: She struggled to follow the pace of the group in her first class.
p2.ex1: He learned to follow the pace of the instructor during the session.
p2.ex2: Do not worry about following the pace at first — focus on technique.

p2.ru: в течение многих лет / ещё долгие годы
p2.en: For a long time in the future.
p2.example: The habits you build now will benefit your health for years to come.
p2.ex1: She hoped to stay active for years to come.
p2.ex2: Good sleep habits formed now will help you for years to come.

p2.en: Every day; as part of a regular daily routine.
p2.example: She exercises on a daily basis and has done so for five years.
p2.ex1: He tracks his steps on a daily basis using a fitness app.
p2.ex2: Drinking enough water on a daily basis is essential for good health.

p3.en: A single person, considered separately from a group.
p3.example: Each individual responds differently to the same fitness programme.
p3.ex1: The trainer adapted the plan for each individual in the group.
p3.ex2: As an individual, she preferred working out alone rather than in a team.

p3.en: In a different situation; if not.
p3.example: Stick to your routine; otherwise, the habit will quickly fade.
p3.ex1: She set a reminder; otherwise she would forget to take her vitamins.
p3.ex2: Exercise regularly; otherwise your fitness level will decline rapidly.

p3.en: Designed or adapted for a specific person.
p3.example: A personalised fitness plan is more effective than a generic one.
p3.ex1: She received a personalised nutrition plan from her dietitian.
p3.ex2: He preferred personalised coaching to group sessions.

p3.en: The advantages and disadvantages of something.
p3.example: She weighed up the pros and cons of joining a gym versus exercising at home.
p3.ex1: There are pros and cons to every type of diet.
p3.ex2: He listed the pros and cons before choosing his training programme.

p3.en: To help people know more about an important issue.
p3.example: The campaign aims to raise awareness about the importance of mental health.
p3.ex1: She organised a community event to raise awareness of poor diet habits.
p3.ex2: The school raised awareness about screen time and sleep quality.

p3.en: To cause a particular outcome.
p3.example: Consistent effort results in long-lasting improvement.
p3.ex1: Skipping meals regularly can result in nutritional deficiencies.
p3.ex2: His dedication to training resulted in a personal best time.

p3.en: A person who is on the same team as you.
p3.example: Her teammate encouraged her to keep going during the final lap.
p3.ex1: He trusted his teammate to maintain the pace during the relay.
p3.ex2: Good communication between teammates improves team performance.

p3.en: A general direction in which something is developing or changing.
p3.example: The trend towards home workouts increased significantly in recent years.
p3.ex1: She does not follow every fitness trend — she sticks to what works.
p3.ex2: The trend of mindful eating has grown in popularity worldwide.

p3.en: A person who uses a product, service, or tool.
p3.example: The fitness app has over a million active users worldwide.
p3.ex1: Users of the platform can track their steps and calorie intake.
p3.ex2: She was a long-term user of the nutrition tracking app.

p3.en: Taking everything into account; considering everything together.
p3.example: All in all, the new routine was a great success after the first month.
p3.ex1: All in all, she felt healthier and happier than she had in years.
p3.ex2: All in all, the programme had more benefits than drawbacks.

p3.en: Used to give your personal opinion on a topic.
p3.example: From my point of view, consistency matters more than intensity.
p3.ex1: From my point of view, rest days are just as important as training days.
p3.ex2: From my point of view, the best habit is one you can sustain long-term.

p3.en: In addition; used to add a stronger or more important point.
p3.example: Exercise improves mood; furthermore, it increases energy levels throughout the day.
p3.ex1: She exercises regularly; furthermore, she maintains a balanced diet.
p3.ex2: The plan is effective; furthermore, it is easy to follow.

p3.en: Used to express a personal opinion.
p3.example: In my view, sleep is the most underrated pillar of good health.
p3.ex1: In my view, small habits done consistently beat intense bursts of effort.
p3.ex2: In my view, finding exercise you enjoy is the most important factor.

p3.en: Used to refer to the specific situation being discussed.
p3.example: In this case, the best approach is to reduce intensity and focus on recovery.
p3.ex1: In this case, a visit to the doctor is the most sensible option.
p3.ex2: In this case, starting slowly and building up is the wisest choice.

p3.ru: и последнее, но не менее важное
p3.en: Used to introduce the final point, emphasising that it is just as important.
p3.example: Last but not least, make sure you drink enough water every single day.
p3.ex1: Last but not least, rest is just as important as training.
p3.ex2: Last but not least, consistency is the key to lasting health.

p3.en: In addition to what has been said; introducing a stronger further point.
p3.example: Exercise boosts mood; moreover, it reduces the risk of serious illness.
p3.ex1: She sleeps well; moreover, she wakes up feeling energised.
p3.ex2: The method is simple; moreover, it has been scientifically proven to work.

p3.en: Used to introduce a contrasting point of view or fact.
p3.example: Gym memberships can be expensive; on the other hand, the facilities are excellent.
p3.ex1: Running is free; on the other hand, it can be hard on the joints.
p3.ex2: The diet is strict; on the other hand, it produces fast results.

p3.ru: в целом / в общем и целом
p3.en: Taking everything into account; generally speaking.
p3.example: On the whole, people who exercise regularly report higher levels of happiness.
p3.ex1: On the whole, her new routine was more effective than the previous one.
p3.ex2: On the whole, the research supports the benefits of regular movement.

p3.en: Used to introduce a brief summary of what has been said.
p3.example: To sum up, building good habits takes time, effort, and patience.
p3.ex1: To sum up, the key to health is consistency, not perfection.
p3.ex2: To sum up, the programme was beneficial for all participants.

p1.en: The power or skill to do something.
p1.example: Humans have the ability to adapt, but natural disasters test that ability severely.
p1.ex1: She has the ability to stay calm in emergency situations.
p1.ex2: The community showed an impressive ability to recover after the flood.

p1.en: To go somewhere with someone; to happen at the same time as something.
p1.example: Heavy rainfall often accompanies tropical storms.
p1.ex1: Flooding usually accompanies severe hurricanes in coastal areas.
p1.ex2: A team of volunteers accompanied the rescue workers to the disaster zone.

p1.en: To do something; to take action in response to a situation.
p1.example: Emergency services must act quickly when a wildfire spreads.
p1.ex1: She acted fast to save her belongings before the flood reached her home.
p1.ex2: Governments must act now to prepare for future natural disasters.

p1.en: In opposition to something; in the direction that opposes something.
p1.example: People are largely powerless against the force of a tsunami.
p1.ex1: Communities must work together against the threat of wildfires.
p1.ex2: Barriers were built to protect the town against flooding.

p1.en: To give a part towards a result or effort.
p1.example: Deforestation contributes to the increased frequency of wildfires.
p1.ex1: Everyone can contribute to disaster relief in some way.
p1.ex2: Climate change contributes to the growing severity of droughts.

p1.en: Harmed or broken, especially by a disaster or accident.
p1.example: Hundreds of homes were damaged by the earthquake.
p1.ex1: The damaged bridge could not be used for weeks after the flood.
p1.ex2: She returned to find her property badly damaged by the wildfire.

p1.en: To damage something so completely that it no longer exists or works.
p1.example: The earthquake destroyed thousands of homes in the region.
p1.ex1: The wildfire destroyed large areas of forest within hours.
p1.ex2: Floods can destroy crops and leave communities without food.

p1.en: A long period of time when there is little or no rain.
p1.example: The severe drought left farmers unable to grow crops for two seasons.
p1.ex1: A prolonged drought caused water shortages across the country.
p1.ex2: The drought was so extreme that rivers dried up completely.

p1.en: A sudden, violent shaking of the ground caused by movement beneath the surface.
p1.example: The earthquake measured 7.2 on the Richter scale and caused widespread damage.
p1.ex1: Many buildings collapsed during the earthquake because they were poorly constructed.
p1.ex2: After the earthquake, rescue teams searched for survivors in the rubble.

p1.en: Very large in size, amount, or degree.
p1.example: The tsunami caused enormous damage to the coastal towns.
p1.ex1: An enormous wildfire burned for weeks before it was contained.
p1.ex2: The cost of rebuilding after the flood was enormous.

p1.en: A person whose job is catching fish.
p1.example: Local fishermen were among the first to notice the unusual drop in sea levels before the tsunami.
p1.ex1: The fisherman was rescued from his boat after the sudden storm.
p1.ex2: Many fishermen lost their equipment and boats in the flood.

p1.en: A large net used to catch fish in the sea or a river.
p1.example: Fishing nets tangled with debris were found washed ashore after the tsunami.
p1.ex1: She photographed a fishing net full of plastic waste on the beach.
p1.ex2: The fishermen lost their fishing nets in the storm.

p1.en: A hot, bright stream of burning gas produced by a fire.
p1.example: The flames spread rapidly through the dry forest during the heatwave.
p1.ex1: Firefighters battled the flames for twelve hours before controlling the wildfire.
p1.ex2: She could see the orange flames from miles away.

p1.en: A large amount of water covering an area that is usually dry.
p1.example: The flood destroyed crops and left thousands of people homeless.
p1.ex1: Emergency services evacuated residents before the flood reached the town.
p1.ex2: The flood waters rose rapidly overnight, catching many families off guard.

p1.en: All the businesses involved in producing or processing a particular type of product.
p1.example: Heavy industry along the river has contributed to severe water pollution.
p1.ex1: The fishing industry was devastated by the oil spill.
p1.ex2: Local industry was forced to shut down during the flood.

p1.en: To cause the death of a person, animal, or plant.
p1.example: The earthquake killed over a thousand people and injured many more.
p1.ex1: The drought killed livestock and left farmers without income.
p1.ex2: Wildfires kill wildlife and destroy natural habitats.

p1.en: Tiny particles of plastic that pollute the environment, especially oceans.
p1.example: Microplastics have been found in fish, drinking water, and even human blood.
p1.ex1: Scientists are studying the long-term effects of microplastics on marine life.
p1.ex2: Reducing single-use plastics helps lower the amount of microplastics in the ocean.

p1.en: A catastrophic event caused by natural processes of the Earth.
p1.example: A natural disaster can destroy years of development in a matter of hours.
p1.ex1: The government set up an emergency fund to respond to natural disasters.
p1.ex2: Communities near the coast are most vulnerable to natural disasters.

p1.en: All the people living in a particular place.
p1.example: The entire population of the coastal village was evacuated before the tsunami.
p1.ex1: The flood displaced a large portion of the local population.
p1.ex2: A growing population puts more pressure on natural resources.

p1.en: Lacking the ability to control or prevent something.
p1.example: Residents felt completely powerless as the floodwaters rose around them.
p1.ex1: She was powerless to stop the wildfire from reaching her property.
p1.ex2: People are often powerless against sudden natural disasters.

p1.en: To say what you think will happen in the future.
p1.example: Scientists can now predict earthquakes with greater accuracy than before.
p1.ex1: It is difficult to predict exactly when and where a tsunami will strike.
p1.ex2: Meteorologists predicted the severe storm three days in advance.

p1.en: A building or land belonging to someone; also objects owned by a person.
p1.example: Thousands of dollars worth of property was destroyed by the wildfire.
p1.ex1: Insurance companies received thousands of claims for damaged property.
p1.ex2: People were told to leave their property immediately and evacuate.

p1.en: To stop a fire from burning.
p1.example: Firefighters worked through the night to put out the wildfire.
p1.ex1: It took three days to put out the fire that destroyed the forest.
p1.ex2: He used a bucket of water to put out the small fire in the garden.

p1.en: The amount of rain that falls in a particular area over a period of time.
p1.example: Unusually heavy rainfall caused rivers to overflow and flood nearby towns.
p1.ex1: The region experienced record rainfall last autumn.
p1.ex2: Low rainfall over two years led to a severe drought.

p1.en: To identify something from past experience; to acknowledge something as true.
p1.example: Scientists recognise climate change as the main driver of more frequent disasters.
p1.ex1: She recognised the signs of a flash flood and moved to higher ground.
p1.ex2: Governments must recognise the need for better disaster preparedness.

p1.en: To move to a different place.
p1.example: Thousands of families were forced to relocate after the earthquake destroyed their homes.
p1.ex1: The government offered financial help for those who needed to relocate.
p1.ex2: She had to relocate her business after the flood damaged her premises.

p1.en: Very bad, intense, or extreme.
p1.example: The severe drought affected millions of people across three countries.
p1.ex1: She was caught in a severe storm while hiking in the mountains.
p1.ex2: The severe earthquake left the city without water or electricity for days.

p1.en: Something that shows that a particular thing exists or is likely to happen.
p1.example: A sudden drop in sea level is a warning sign of an approaching tsunami.
p1.ex1: Dark skies and strong winds are signs of an incoming storm.
p1.ex2: Scientists monitor warning signs before predicting volcanic eruptions.

p1.en: A way of solving a problem or dealing with a difficult situation.
p1.example: There is no single solution to the growing problem of climate change.
p1.ex1: International cooperation is essential for finding a solution to flooding.
p1.ex2: She proposed a practical solution to reduce the risk of wildfires.

p1.en: To move or cause something to cover a wider area.
p1.example: The wildfire spread rapidly due to strong winds and dry conditions.
p1.ex1: Disease can spread quickly in areas affected by floods.
p1.ex2: Rumours about the earthquake spread on social media before official news.

p1.en: Happening or done quickly and unexpectedly.
p1.example: A sudden change in weather can turn a manageable storm into a disaster.
p1.ex1: The sudden earthquake gave residents no time to evacuate.
p1.ex2: She was shocked by the sudden rise in floodwaters overnight.

p1.en: Making you feel very frightened.
p1.example: Survivors described the moment the tsunami hit as absolutely terrifying.
p1.ex1: It was terrifying to watch the wildfire approach the town.
p1.ex2: The sound of the earthquake was terrifying — like a deep roar from underground.

p1.en: Very sad, especially because involving death or suffering.
p1.example: The earthquake had tragic consequences, with hundreds of lives lost.
p1.ex1: It was tragic to see entire communities destroyed in a single day.
p1.ex2: She described the loss of her home as a tragic experience.

p1.en: An extremely large and powerful wave caused by an underwater earthquake.
p1.example: The tsunami reached the coastline within minutes of the earthquake.
p1.ex1: Warning systems were installed to alert coastal areas of approaching tsunamis.
p1.ex2: The tsunami devastated the fishing village, leaving nothing standing.

p1.en: A piece of new or more recent information about something.
p1.example: Emergency updates were broadcast every hour during the wildfire.
p1.ex1: She checked her phone constantly for updates about the flood.
p1.ex2: The government issued regular updates on the earthquake rescue operation.

p1.en: Absolutely necessary and essential for survival or success.
p1.example: Clean water is vital for survival in the aftermath of a natural disaster.
p1.ex1: Vital information about evacuation routes was broadcast on local radio.
p1.ex2: It is vital that communities prepare emergency kits before disaster strikes.

p1.en: Anything or everything; no matter what.
p1.example: Whatever happens, emergency services will do their best to help everyone.
p1.ex1: She was determined to protect her family, whatever it took.
p1.ex2: Whatever the cause, the community came together to rebuild.

p1.en: A large fire that spreads quickly and is difficult to control, usually in forests or grasslands.
p1.example: The wildfire burned over 10,000 hectares of forest before rain helped contain it.
p1.ex1: Dry summer conditions increase the risk of wildfires significantly.
p1.ex2: She volunteered to help communities rebuild after the wildfire destroyed their homes.

p1.en: To lose your home, usually as a result of a disaster.
p1.example: Over five thousand families were left homeless after the earthquake.
p1.ex1: The floods left thousands of people homeless overnight.
p1.ex2: Aid organisations provided shelter for those left homeless by the wildfire.

p1.en: To be included in something; to belong to a group or process.
p1.example: Volunteering to help with disaster relief means being part of something meaningful.
p1.ex1: She was proud to be part of the rescue team.
p1.ex2: Being part of a community means supporting each other in emergencies.

p1.en: To be extremely expensive.
p1.example: Rebuilding after a major earthquake can cost a fortune.
p1.ex1: The repairs to the flood-damaged bridge cost a fortune.
p1.ex2: Replacing all the damaged property after the wildfire cost a fortune.

p1.en: In a sudden, serious situation that requires immediate action.
p1.example: In an emergency, always call the local disaster hotline first.
p1.ex1: She kept a torch and a first-aid kit in her car in an emergency.
p1.ex2: In an emergency, stay calm and follow the instructions of rescue workers.

p1.en: As a precaution against something happening.
p1.example: In case of flooding, move valuable items to higher floors immediately.
p1.ex1: Prepare an emergency bag in case of evacuation.
p1.ex2: In case of an earthquake, stand under a sturdy doorframe.

p1.en: To not take something with you when you go; to go faster than others.
p1.example: Many people had to leave behind everything they owned when evacuating.
p1.ex1: She left behind her documents when she fled the flood.
p1.ex2: Rescue workers could not leave anyone behind in the disaster zone.

p1.en: To prevent someone from dying.
p1.example: The early warning system saved hundreds of lives before the tsunami struck.
p1.ex1: Her quick thinking saved her neighbour's life during the flood.
p1.ex2: The rescue team saved the life of a child trapped under the rubble.

p2.en: To start using a new method, idea, or way of living.
p2.example: More people are adopting eco-friendly habits to reduce their carbon footprint.
p2.ex1: The school adopted a no-single-use-plastic policy.
p2.ex2: She adopted a more sustainable lifestyle after learning about climate change.

p2.en: To be in a situation where something can affect you.
p2.example: People living near factories are often exposed to toxic fumes.
p2.ex1: Children should not be exposed to harmful chemicals.
p2.ex2: He was exposed to air pollution every day on his commute to work.

p2.en: To decompose or stop working.
p2.example: Plastic does not break down naturally and stays in the environment for centuries.
p2.ex1: Food waste breaks down in a compost bin and becomes fertiliser.
p2.ex2: The old machine broke down and started leaking harmful chemicals.

p2.en: To be on fire or to destroy something with fire.
p2.example: Burning fossil fuels releases greenhouse gases into the atmosphere.
p2.ex1: Many countries burn waste in landfills, which causes air pollution.
p2.ex2: She chose not to burn garden waste and composted it instead.

p2.ru: ездить в машине вместе / организовывать совместные поездки
p2.en: To share a car journey with others to reduce costs and emissions.
p2.example: She started to carpool with colleagues to reduce her carbon footprint.
p2.ex1: Carpooling reduces the number of vehicles on the road.
p2.ex2: They agreed to carpool to work three days a week.

p2.en: To convert food or garden waste into compost by allowing it to decay.
p2.example: She composted all her kitchen waste to fertilise her garden naturally.
p2.ex1: Composting food scraps reduces the amount of waste sent to landfill.
p2.ex2: He set up a compost bin in his garden last spring.

p2.en: To protect something from waste, harm, or overuse.
p2.example: Turning off taps while brushing your teeth helps conserve water.
p2.ex1: She taught her children to conserve energy by switching off lights.
p2.ex2: National parks help conserve natural habitats and wildlife.

p2.en: Making it hard to concentrate on something.
p2.example: Constant notifications about environmental disasters can be distracting and overwhelming.
p2.ex1: She found the noise from the nearby construction distracting.
p2.ex2: He turned off the news because the constant updates were distracting.

p2.en: To give something, especially money or goods, to help a cause.
p2.example: She donated old clothes to a second-hand shop instead of throwing them away.
p2.ex1: He donated a portion of his salary to an environmental charity.
p2.ex2: Many people donate reusable items rather than sending them to landfill.

p2.en: To produce and send out a substance, especially into the atmosphere.
p2.example: Cars emit exhaust fumes that contribute to air pollution and global warming.
p2.ex1: Factories emit greenhouse gases that accelerate climate change.
p2.ex2: The power plant emits large amounts of carbon dioxide every day.

p2.en: Thick cloud at a low level that makes it hard to see.
p2.example: Smog is a type of fog caused by heavy air pollution in cities.
p2.ex1: The thick fog made driving conditions extremely dangerous.
p2.ex2: Industrial fog in the valley was caused by emissions from local factories.

p2.en: Relating to people or human beings.
p2.example: Human activity is the main cause of global warming.
p2.ex1: The human impact on the environment has increased dramatically.
p2.ex2: She believes human behaviour must change to address the climate crisis.

p2.en: A site where waste material is buried or deposited.
p2.example: Millions of tonnes of plastic end up in landfill every year.
p2.ex1: Composting and recycling reduce the amount of waste sent to landfill.
p2.ex2: The government plans to ban single-use plastics to reduce landfill waste.

p2.en: To allow a liquid or gas to escape through a hole or crack.
p2.example: Industrial chemicals leaked into the river, killing fish and other wildlife.
p2.ex1: The old pipe leaked oil into the soil for months before it was detected.
p2.ex2: Toxic gases leaked from the factory during the accident.

p2.en: Rubbish that has been left in a public place.
p2.example: Litter on beaches causes harm to marine animals.
p2.ex1: She organised a local campaign to clean up litter in the park.
p2.ex2: Dropping litter in public places is illegal in many countries.

p2.en: To have a significant positive effect.
p2.example: Small everyday actions like recycling really can make a difference.
p2.ex1: She believed that one person could make a difference in the fight against pollution.
p2.ex2: Donating to environmental charities can make a real difference.

p2.en: To lift and collect something from the ground.
p2.example: She joined a local group that picks up litter along the beach every weekend.
p2.ex1: He picked up the plastic bottles he found on the hiking trail.
p2.ex2: Volunteers picked up over two tonnes of litter from the park.

p2.en: To make air, water, or soil dirty and harmful.
p2.example: Industrial waste has polluted the river for decades.
p2.ex1: Cars pollute the air and contribute to respiratory diseases.
p2.ex2: She was shocked to learn how badly the local water supply had been polluted.

p2.en: The action of stopping something from happening.
p2.example: Prevention of pollution is more effective than trying to clean it up later.
p2.ex1: Flood prevention involves building barriers and improving drainage systems.
p2.ex2: Environmental prevention programmes focus on reducing emissions at source.

p2.en: Designed to be used more than once.
p2.example: Switching to reusable bags and bottles is a simple way to reduce plastic waste.
p2.ex1: She always carries a reusable water bottle instead of buying plastic ones.
p2.ex2: Reusable packaging is becoming more popular in supermarkets.

p2.en: To use something again rather than throwing it away.
p2.example: Try to reuse packaging materials instead of putting them in the bin.
p2.ex1: She reused glass jars as containers for herbs and spices.
p2.ex2: The company encourages customers to reuse bags when they shop.

p2.en: Goods previously owned by someone else; a shop that sells used items.
p2.example: Buying clothes from a second-hand shop reduces the demand for fast fashion.
p2.ex1: She found a great jacket at the local second-hand shop for a fraction of the price.
p2.ex2: He donated his old furniture to a second-hand shop rather than throwing it away.

p2.en: Designed to be used once and then thrown away.
p2.example: Single-use plastics are one of the biggest contributors to ocean pollution.
p2.ex1: She replaced all single-use cups at work with reusable mugs.
p2.ex2: Many countries have banned single-use plastic bags.

p2.en: The grey or black gas produced when something burns.
p2.example: Thick smoke from wildfires caused serious air quality problems across the region.
p2.ex1: Industrial smoke from the factory was visible from several kilometres away.
p2.ex2: She closed the windows to stop the smoke from entering the house.

p2.en: The community of people living in a particular country or region.
p2.example: Society as a whole must take responsibility for tackling climate change.
p2.ex1: She believes that society needs to change its relationship with plastic.
p2.ex2: Modern society produces far more waste than can be safely managed.

p2.en: To arrange things into groups or categories.
p2.example: She sorts her waste into recycling, compost, and general rubbish every week.
p2.ex1: Sorting plastic from paper and glass makes recycling more effective.
p2.ex2: He taught his children to sort their rubbish from an early age.

p2.en: To do something in response to a problem or situation.
p2.example: We must take action now to reduce carbon emissions before it is too late.
p2.ex1: She decided to take action by starting a community recycling programme.
p2.ex2: World leaders were urged to take action on climate change at the summit.

p2.en: A machine with an engine used to transport people or goods.
p2.example: Electric vehicles produce no exhaust fumes and help reduce air pollution.
p2.ex1: The number of vehicles on the road has tripled in the last thirty years.
p2.ex2: She switched from a petrol vehicle to an electric one to reduce her emissions.

p2.en: Different types of pollution affecting different parts of the environment.
p2.example: Marine pollution from plastic waste is one of the most urgent environmental issues.
p2.ex1: Noise pollution in cities affects sleep quality and mental health.
p2.ex2: Soil pollution caused by industrial chemicals harms crops and wildlife.

p2.en: The total amount of greenhouse gases produced by a person, organisation, or activity.
p2.example: She calculated her carbon footprint and decided to fly less and cycle more.
p2.ex1: Eating less meat is one of the most effective ways to reduce your carbon footprint.
p2.ex2: Companies are under pressure to reduce their carbon footprint.

p2.en: Key collocations about the environment and its problems.
p2.example: Raising environmental awareness is the first step towards changing behaviour.
p2.ex1: The oil spill was an environmental disaster that affected thousands of species.
p2.ex2: The environmental impact of flying once equals driving for months.

p2.en: Collocations describing whether something helps or harms the environment.
p2.example: She switched to environmentally friendly cleaning products.
p2.ex1: Single-use plastics are environmentally harmful and should be avoided.
p2.ex2: The packaging is certified as environmentally safe.

p2.en: Gases produced by the engine of a vehicle that pollute the air.
p2.example: Children who live near busy roads are regularly exposed to exhaust fumes.
p2.ex1: Exhaust fumes from lorries contribute significantly to air pollution in cities.
p2.ex2: Electric vehicles do not emit exhaust fumes.

p2.en: Food that is discarded or not consumed.
p2.example: One third of all food produced globally ends up as food waste.
p2.ex1: She started meal planning to reduce food waste at home.
p2.ex2: Composting food waste is better than sending it to landfill.

p2.en: Natural fuels such as coal, oil, and gas formed from ancient organisms.
p2.example: Burning fossil fuels is the leading cause of greenhouse gas emissions.
p2.ex1: Many countries are trying to reduce their dependence on fossil fuels.
p2.ex2: She supports the transition away from fossil fuels to renewable energy.

p2.en: The gradual increase in the overall temperature of the Earth.
p2.example: Global warming is causing ice caps to melt and sea levels to rise.
p2.ex1: Scientists agree that global warming is largely caused by human activity.
p2.ex2: Reducing emissions is essential to slow the pace of global warming.

p2.en: Gases like CO2 that trap heat in the atmosphere, causing warming.
p2.example: The greenhouse effect is a natural process, but human activity has intensified it.
p2.ex1: Greenhouse gases from industry and transport are a major environmental issue.
p2.ex2: She learned about the greenhouse effect in her environmental science class.

p2.en: A bulb that uses less electricity than a traditional one.
p2.example: Switching to energy-saving light bulbs reduces both electricity use and bills.
p2.ex1: She replaced every bulb in her house with an energy-saving one.
p2.ex2: Energy-saving light bulbs last much longer than traditional ones.

p2.en: The natural environment where a species lives; materials found in nature.
p2.example: Deforestation destroys the natural habitat of countless species.
p2.ex1: Sustainable farming helps preserve natural resources for future generations.
p2.ex2: Many animals are losing their natural habitat due to human development.

p2.en: A facility that generates electricity, often by burning fuel.
p2.example: Coal-fired power plants are one of the biggest sources of air pollution.
p2.ex1: The government plans to close the last coal power plant by 2030.
p2.ex2: She campaigned against the building of a new power plant near the town.

p2.en: A part of a town or city where people live rather than work.
p2.example: Air quality in residential areas near industrial zones is often very poor.
p2.ex1: The new recycling centre will be built away from residential areas.
p2.ex2: Noise pollution is a growing problem in residential areas near airports.

p2.en: Technology that uses energy from the sun.
p2.example: She installed solar panels on the roof to generate clean electricity.
p2.ex1: Solar power is one of the fastest-growing sources of renewable energy.
p2.ex2: The school switched to solar heating to reduce its energy bills.

p2.en: Energy from sources that are naturally replenished.
p2.example: Investing in renewable energy is essential to reduce dependence on fossil fuels.
p2.ex1: Wind energy has grown significantly as a source of alternative power.
p2.ex2: She researched different types of renewable energy for her school project.

p2.en: Poisonous gases or substances that are harmful to health.
p2.example: Workers in the factory were exposed to toxic fumes without proper protection.
p2.ex1: Toxic chemicals leaked into the groundwater from the old industrial site.
p2.ex2: Burning rubbish in the open releases toxic gases into the air.

p2.en: Different categories of waste that require careful handling.
p2.example: Industrial waste must be disposed of safely to prevent soil and water pollution.
p2.ex1: Household waste can be reduced by composting and recycling.
p2.ex2: Chemical waste from laboratories must be treated before disposal.

p2.en: An insufficient supply of water or food.
p2.example: Climate change is expected to cause severe water shortages in many regions.
p2.ex1: The drought led to a critical food shortage across the affected areas.
p2.ex2: Aid organisations responded quickly to the water shortage after the earthquake.

p1.en: Used to show that a figure is not exact; roughly.
p1.example: Approximately one third of all mammal species are currently threatened with extinction.
p1.ex1: The whale shark can grow to approximately twelve metres in length.
p1.ex2: Approximately five hundred tigers remain in the wild in India.

p1.en: An act of trying to do something, especially something difficult.
p1.example: This is the third attempt to reintroduce wolves to the national park.
p1.ex1: Her attempt to raise funds for the conservation project was successful.
p1.ex2: Despite several attempts, scientists have been unable to save the species from extinction.

p1.en: The protection and preservation of the natural environment.
p1.example: Wildlife conservation is essential for maintaining the balance of ecosystems.
p1.ex1: She dedicated her career to the conservation of endangered marine species.
p1.ex2: Conservation efforts have helped the giant panda recover from near-extinction.

p1.en: A person who works to protect the natural environment.
p1.example: The conservationist spent twenty years protecting the mountain gorilla population.
p1.ex1: She became a conservationist after witnessing the destruction of a coral reef.
p1.ex2: Local conservationists are working to protect the last remaining wolves in the region.

p1.en: Physical harm caused to something; the harm done to something or someone.
p1.example: The oil spill caused irreversible damage to the local marine ecosystem.
p1.ex1: Deforestation causes enormous damage to natural habitats and biodiversity.
p1.ex2: The damage to coral reefs from rising sea temperatures is severe.

p1.en: A reduction in amount or size; to become smaller or fewer.
p1.example: Scientists have recorded a significant decrease in the global bee population.
p1.ex1: The number of wild tigers decreased dramatically during the twentieth century.
p1.ex2: Conservation programmes have helped decrease the rate of species extinction.

p1.en: To fall or decrease suddenly.
p1.example: The rhino population dropped to fewer than one hundred individuals at its lowest point.
p1.ex1: Temperatures dropped sharply, threatening the nesting sites of sea turtles.
p1.ex2: Fish stocks dropped to dangerously low levels due to overfishing.

p1.uz: yo'q bo'lib ketish xavfi ostidagi tur
p1.en: A type of animal or plant at serious risk of extinction.
p1.example: The amur leopard is one of the most critically endangered species on Earth.
p1.ex1: Governments must pass laws to protect endangered species from hunting.
p1.ex2: She volunteered at a rescue centre for endangered species.

p1.en: To make certain that something happens or is the case.
p1.example: Strict laws are needed to ensure the survival of endangered species.
p1.ex1: The conservation programme works to ensure wolves can live safely in the wild.
p1.ex2: She campaigned to ensure the government funded wildlife protection.

p1.en: No longer in existence; having died out completely.
p1.example: The dodo became extinct in the seventeenth century due to hunting.
p1.ex1: Scientists fear that several more species could become extinct within a decade.
p1.ex2: Once a species is extinct, it can never be brought back.

p1.en: The state of a species no longer existing anywhere on Earth.
p1.example: Human activity is the leading cause of the current mass extinction of wildlife.
p1.ex1: The extinction of the woolly mammoth was partly caused by climate change.
p1.ex2: Conservation efforts aim to prevent the extinction of the snow leopard.

p1.en: The group of people responsible for running a country or region.
p1.example: The government announced new legislation to protect endangered species.
p1.ex1: She lobbied the government to increase funding for marine conservation.
p1.ex2: The government banned all forms of ivory trading to protect elephants.

p1.en: To chase and kill wild animals, especially for sport or food.
p1.example: Poachers continue to hunt elephants illegally for their ivory.
p1.ex1: Wolves were hunted to near-extinction across much of Europe.
p1.ex2: It is illegal to hunt protected species in most countries.

p1.en: The activity of chasing and killing wild animals.
p1.example: Illegal hunting remains one of the greatest threats to endangered wildlife.
p1.ex1: Trophy hunting has led to the decline of several big cat populations.
p1.ex2: She campaigns against the hunting of whales in international waters.

p1.en: A warm-blooded animal that breathes air, has a backbone, and feeds its young with milk.
p1.example: The blue whale is the largest mammal ever known to have existed.
p1.ex1: Dolphins are highly intelligent marine mammals.
p1.ex2: Many mammal species are currently threatened with extinction.

p1.en: The largest or highest amount that is possible or allowed.
p1.example: The maximum penalty for illegal wildlife trafficking should be increased.
p1.ex1: The reserve can support a maximum of fifty wolves at any one time.
p1.ex2: Scientists recommend a maximum catch limit to prevent overfishing.

p1.en: To change from a solid to a liquid because of heat.
p1.example: As Arctic ice melts due to global warming, polar bear habitats are disappearing.
p1.ex1: Glaciers are melting at a faster rate than at any point in recorded history.
p1.ex2: The permafrost is melting, releasing greenhouse gases into the atmosphere.

p1.en: The smallest or lowest amount that is possible or required.
p1.example: A minimum of two thousand individuals is needed for a species to survive long-term.
p1.ex1: The government set a minimum protected area for the species to breed.
p1.ex2: Scientists say the minimum viable population of tigers is around three hundred.

p1.en: An accidental release of oil into the sea or environment.
p1.example: The oil spill caused the deaths of thousands of seabirds and marine animals.
p1.ex1: Cleanup operations following the oil spill lasted for over a year.
p1.ex2: The oil spill devastated the coastline and destroyed fishing livelihoods.

p1.en: Not complete; affecting only part of something.
p1.example: The conservation programme achieved partial success in increasing the whale population.
p1.ex1: A partial ban on fishing was introduced to protect the coral reef.
p1.ex2: There was only a partial recovery of the fish population after the pollution event.

p1.en: The act of keeping someone or something safe from harm.
p1.example: Legal protection is essential for endangered species to recover.
p1.ex1: She campaigned for stronger protection of rainforest habitats.
p1.ex2: Without government protection, the species could disappear within a generation.

p1.en: To allow an animal to go free, especially back into the wild.
p1.example: After months of rehabilitation, the sea turtle was released back into the ocean.
p1.ex1: Scientists released twenty wolves into the national park as part of a rewilding project.
p1.ex2: The injured eagle was released once it had fully recovered.

p1.en: To return something to its original condition or bring it back.
p1.example: The aim is to restore the wetlands that were drained for agriculture.
p1.ex1: Replanting trees helps restore forest ecosystems that were destroyed.
p1.ex2: The conservation team worked to restore the population of the mountain gorilla.

p1.en: The state of continuing to live or exist, especially in difficult conditions.
p1.example: The survival of the species depends on protecting its natural habitat.
p1.ex1: She dedicated her research to understanding the survival rates of sea turtle eggs.
p1.ex2: Without clean water, the survival of many species is at risk.

p1.en: The quality of being significant or necessary.
p1.example: She emphasised the importance of international cooperation in wildlife conservation.
p1.ex1: The importance of protecting natural habitats cannot be overstated.
p1.ex2: He spoke about the importance of reducing plastic pollution in the ocean.

p1.en: Kept in a controlled environment such as a zoo, rather than living in the wild.
p1.example: Giant pandas have been successfully bred in captivity as part of conservation programmes.
p1.ex1: Animals in captivity often struggle to survive when released into the wild.
p1.ex2: The last known individual of the species died in captivity in 2018.

p1.en: In a natural environment, free from human control.
p1.example: There are fewer than four hundred Amur leopards left in the wild.
p1.ex1: Many species can only survive in the wild if their habitats are protected.
p1.ex2: Scientists track the movements of wolves in the wild using GPS collars.

p1.en: The fact of no longer having something; a reduction or disappearance.
p1.example: The loss of biodiversity is one of the most serious environmental crises of our time.
p1.ex1: The loss of the rainforest means the loss of thousands of species.
p1.ex2: She wrote about the loss of coral reefs due to ocean warming.

p1.en: Something that is likely to cause harm or damage.
p1.example: Climate change poses the greatest threat to biodiversity in the coming decades.
p1.ex1: Poaching remains a serious threat to elephant populations across Africa.
p1.ex2: Plastic pollution is a growing threat to marine life worldwide.

p2.en: A law passed by a government; also a single action or deed.
p2.example: The Clean Air Act introduced stricter limits on industrial emissions.
p2.ex1: The government passed an act to ban the use of fossil fuels in new buildings.
p2.ex2: Each act of recycling contributes to a cleaner environment.

p2.en: Cheap enough for people to be able to buy.
p2.example: Solar panels have become much more affordable over the past decade.
p2.ex1: The government subsidised electric cars to make them more affordable.
p2.ex2: She looked for affordable ways to reduce her household energy use.

p2.en: An organised series of actions aimed at achieving a goal.
p2.example: The environmental campaign successfully raised awareness about wind farm benefits.
p2.ex1: She launched a campaign to get the city council to install more solar panels.
p2.ex2: The campaign collected over a million signatures against the power plant.

p2.en: Happening or continuing all the time without stopping.
p2.example: Wind turbines require a constant supply of wind to generate electricity.
p2.ex1: She found the constant noise from the wind farm distracting.
p2.ex2: Constant exposure to exhaust fumes can cause serious respiratory problems.

p2.en: The natural light that comes from the sun during the day.
p2.example: Solar panels generate the most electricity during hours of daylight.
p2.ex1: She adjusted her routine to make the most of daylight for her solar heating.
p2.ex2: During winter, there are fewer hours of daylight for solar panels to operate.

p2.en: The process of cutting down all the trees in a large area of forest.
p2.example: Deforestation in the Amazon is destroying biodiversity at an alarming rate.
p2.ex1: She joined a campaign to stop deforestation and protect the rainforest.
p2.ex2: Deforestation contributes significantly to greenhouse gas emissions.

p2.en: To interrupt or cause problems for someone or something.
p2.example: Wind turbines can disturb local wildlife, particularly birds and bats.
p2.ex1: Construction work disturbed the natural habitat of several bird species.
p2.ex2: She was concerned that the new road would disturb the ecosystem.

p2.en: All the living things in an area together with the environment they interact with.
p2.example: Destroying a forest damages the entire ecosystem that depends on it.
p2.ex1: The oil spill devastated the marine ecosystem in the bay.
p2.ex2: Bees are vital to the ecosystem because they pollinate plants.

p2.en: A car powered by electricity rather than petrol or diesel.
p2.example: Electric cars produce no exhaust fumes and reduce urban air pollution.
p2.ex1: She switched to an electric car to reduce her carbon footprint.
p2.ex2: Governments are encouraging people to buy electric cars with tax incentives.

p2.en: The activity of growing crops or raising animals for food.
p2.example: Intensive farming is a major driver of soil and water pollution.
p2.ex1: Sustainable farming methods help protect the environment and biodiversity.
p2.ex2: She researched the impact of modern farming on natural habitats.

p2.en: To provide money for a project or activity.
p2.example: The government agreed to fund a major wind farm project off the coast.
p2.ex1: She raised money to fund a conservation project in the rainforest.
p2.ex2: The solar energy initiative was funded by a combination of private and public money.

p2.en: Not likely to cause harm or injury.
p2.example: Wind power is completely harmless to the atmosphere compared to fossil fuels.
p2.ex1: She chose a harmless, eco-friendly cleaning product for her home.
p2.ex2: The substance is harmless to humans but toxic to certain insects.

p2.en: To make something warm or hot.
p2.example: Solar panels can heat water for domestic use at a fraction of the usual cost.
p2.ex1: She uses solar heating to heat her home during the winter months.
p2.ex2: The building is heated entirely by renewable energy.

p2.en: To pay no attention to something; to treat as if it does not exist.
p2.example: We cannot ignore the environmental impact of building new wind farms.
p2.ex1: She was frustrated that the council ignored her concerns about air pollution.
p2.ex2: Governments cannot afford to ignore the threat of climate change any longer.

p2.en: The process of putting equipment in place ready for use.
p2.example: The installation of solar panels on school rooftops has reduced energy costs.
p2.ex1: The installation of wind turbines took several months to complete.
p2.ex2: She supervised the installation of energy-saving lighting in the office.

p2.en: The measurement of something from one end to the other; also the duration of something.
p2.example: The length of the wind farm stretches for over twenty kilometres along the coast.
p2.ex1: The length of time needed to see a return on solar panel investment has decreased.
p2.ex2: Each wind turbine blade reaches a length of over sixty metres.

p2.en: To express an argument or opinion clearly.
p2.example: She made a point of highlighting the long-term benefits of renewable energy.
p2.ex1: He made an important point about the noise pollution caused by wind turbines.
p2.ex2: The campaigner made a compelling point about the cost of inaction on climate change.

p2.en: To work or function; to control the functioning of something.
p2.example: Modern wind turbines can operate efficiently in a wide range of wind speeds.
p2.ex1: The solar farm operates at full capacity during summer.
p2.ex2: She learned how the energy grid operates before joining the environmental team.

p2.en: To supply energy to a machine or system.
p2.example: The wind farm produces enough electricity to power ten thousand homes.
p2.ex1: Solar panels power the entire school, including the heating system.
p2.ex2: She wanted her house to be powered entirely by renewable energy.

p2.en: To cause someone or an animal to feel frightened.
p2.example: Wind turbines can scare birds and disrupt their migration routes.
p2.ex1: The noise from the construction work scared away the nesting birds.
p2.ex2: Opponents of wind farms argue that they scare away wildlife.

p2.en: Making no sound; completely quiet.
p2.example: Electric cars are almost completely silent, reducing noise pollution in cities.
p2.ex1: The solar panels operate silently on the rooftop without any mechanical noise.
p2.ex2: She appreciated how silent the electric engine was compared to her old car.

p2.en: The light that comes directly from the sun.
p2.example: Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity that can power homes.
p2.ex1: The more hours of sunlight a region receives, the more effective solar power is.
p2.ex2: She positioned the solar panels to capture the maximum amount of sunlight.

p2.en: To do things that are intended to deal with a problem or prevent something.
p2.example: Governments must take measures against deforestation before it is too late.
p2.ex1: The city council took measures against air pollution by banning diesel vehicles.
p2.ex2: She urged world leaders to take measures against the rapid rise in global temperatures.

p2.en: In every part of something; during the whole of a period.
p2.example: Wind energy is generated throughout the year, even on cloudy days.
p2.ex1: She campaigned for environmental protection throughout her entire career.
p2.ex2: Renewable energy projects are being developed throughout the country.

p2.en: Unpleasant to look at; not attractive.
p2.example: Some people argue that wind turbines are ugly and spoil the landscape.
p2.ex1: She disagreed that solar panels were ugly and thought they looked modern.
p2.ex2: The opponents called the new power plant ugly and out of place.

p2.en: Not pleasant or appealing to look at.
p2.example: Critics of wind farms consider them unattractive additions to the countryside.
p2.ex1: She found the industrial design of the solar farm unattractive.
p2.ex2: He admitted the turbines were unattractive but argued their benefits outweighed this.

p2.en: Not needed; more than what is required.
p2.example: Switching off lights in empty rooms avoids unnecessary energy waste.
p2.ex1: She avoided unnecessary car journeys by cycling to work.
p2.ex2: The report called the new power plant unnecessary given existing renewable capacity.

p2.ru: отключать от сети / вынимать из розетки
p2.en: To remove an electrical device from its power source.
p2.example: Unplug chargers and appliances when not in use to reduce energy waste.
p2.ex1: She made a habit of unplugging all devices before going to bed.
p2.ex2: He unplugged the television at the wall to avoid standby energy consumption.

p2.en: Relating to a town or city rather than the countryside.
p2.example: Air pollution is a particularly serious problem in densely populated urban areas.
p2.ex1: Solar panels are increasingly common in urban areas.
p2.ex2: She studied the impact of green spaces on well-being in urban environments.

p2.en: A group of wind turbines used to generate electricity.
p2.example: The offshore wind farm can power over a hundred thousand homes.
p2.ex1: Local residents were divided about the plan to build a wind farm nearby.
p2.ex2: She visited a wind farm as part of her research into renewable energy.

p2.en: To start suddenly, especially of fire, disease, or conflict.
p2.example: A wildfire broke out in the dry forest during the heatwave.
p2.ex1: Protests broke out after the government approved the new coal plant.
p2.ex2: A fire broke out at the chemical factory, releasing toxic fumes.

p2.en: To permanently stop operating.
p2.example: The government announced plans to close down all coal-fired power plants by 2030.
p2.ex1: The polluting factory was forced to close down after failing safety inspections.
p2.ex2: She campaigned for the old diesel bus depot to be closed down.

p2.en: To chop a tree; also to reduce the amount of something.
p2.example: Thousands of trees are cut down every day to make way for new farmland.
p2.ex1: She cut down on her energy use by installing a smart thermostat.
p2.ex2: The charity urged people to cut down on meat consumption to reduce emissions.

p2.en: To be powered by a particular fuel or energy source.
p2.example: Her car runs on electricity and produces zero direct emissions.
p2.ex1: The factory now runs on solar power instead of coal.
p2.ex2: She chose a boiler that runs on renewable natural gas.

p2.en: To discard something you no longer need.
p2.example: Instead of throwing out old electronics, consider donating or recycling them.
p2.ex1: She never throws out food — she composts vegetable peelings instead.
p2.ex2: He was about to throw out the old furniture until she suggested giving it away.

p3.en: To take in or soak up a substance or form of energy.
p3.example: Trees absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen, making them vital for the climate.
p3.ex1: Solar panels absorb sunlight and convert it into usable electricity.
p3.ex2: Wetlands absorb floodwater and help prevent towns from flooding.

p3.en: Once a year; every year.
p3.example: Millions of tonnes of plastic enter the ocean annually.
p3.ex1: The city reduces its carbon emissions by approximately five per cent annually.
p3.ex2: She tracks her household energy use annually to measure her progress.

p3.en: A gas produced by burning fossil fuels and by breathing, contributing to global warming.
p3.example: Carbon dioxide is the main greenhouse gas responsible for global warming.
p3.ex1: Trees help reduce the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.
p3.ex2: She monitored the level of carbon dioxide in the building to improve air quality.

p3.en: A place where electric vehicles or devices can be charged.
p3.example: The city council installed new electric vehicle charging stations in every car park.
p3.ex1: She always checks the location of charging stations before a long journey.
p3.ex2: More charging stations are needed to encourage people to switch to electric cars.

p3.en: A strong need or requirement for something.
p3.example: Global demand for energy continues to grow despite climate change concerns.
p3.ex1: The demand for electric cars has increased significantly in recent years.
p3.ex2: She studied how consumer demand is driving the shift to renewable energy.

p3.en: Electronic devices and equipment.
p3.example: Old electronics should be recycled properly to avoid harmful e-waste.
p3.ex1: She donates working electronics to schools rather than throwing them away.
p3.ex2: The production of electronics uses large amounts of rare earth minerals.

p3.en: The production and discharge of a gas or substance into the atmosphere.
p3.example: The government has committed to reducing carbon emissions by fifty per cent by 2035.
p3.ex1: She calculated her annual carbon emissions to identify where to make changes.
p3.ex2: Switching to renewable energy is the most effective way to reduce emissions.

p3.en: Interesting and attractive; holding your attention.
p3.example: The environmental documentary was so engaging that she watched it twice.
p3.ex1: She created an engaging social media campaign to raise awareness of e-waste.
p3.ex2: He gave an engaging presentation on the benefits of solar energy.

p3.en: Discarded electronic devices and components.
p3.example: E-waste is one of the fastest-growing types of waste globally.
p3.ex1: She organised a community e-waste collection drive at the local school.
p3.ex2: Improper disposal of e-waste releases toxic chemicals into the soil.

p3.en: To become or make larger in size, number, or importance.
p3.example: The city plans to expand its network of solar-powered streetlights.
p3.ex1: She helped the charity expand its recycling programme to new districts.
p3.ex2: The government wants to expand the use of renewable energy across all sectors.

p3.en: A market where local farmers sell their produce directly to consumers.
p3.example: Buying food from a farmer's market reduces the emissions from long-distance transport.
p3.ex1: She goes to the farmer's market every Saturday to buy locally grown vegetables.
p3.ex2: Farmer's markets help reduce food miles and support the local economy.

p3.en: Equipment for producing light; the light itself.
p3.example: Switching to LED lighting significantly reduces household electricity consumption.
p3.ex1: The city replaced all street lighting with energy-efficient LED bulbs.
p3.ex2: She improved the lighting in her home and reduced her electricity bill.

p3.en: The action of making something smaller or less.
p3.example: A significant reduction in carbon emissions is needed to limit global warming.
p3.ex1: She celebrated the reduction in household waste after starting to compost.
p3.ex2: The factory achieved a forty per cent reduction in energy use over five years.

p3.en: The act of fixing something that is broken or damaged.
p3.example: Choosing repair over replacement reduces e-waste and saves money.
p3.ex1: She took her broken phone for repair rather than buying a new one.
p3.ex2: The repair of the solar panels took only a few hours.

p3.en: Operated using energy from the sun.
p3.example: The school installed solar-powered streetlights around its campus.
p3.ex1: She drives a solar-powered vehicle on short city journeys.
p3.ex2: The solar-powered building generates more energy than it uses.

p3.en: Lights positioned along roads and streets to illuminate them at night.
p3.example: The city council replaced all old streetlights with solar-powered LED ones.
p3.ex1: New solar-powered streetlights were installed along the main road.
p3.ex2: She proposed replacing the streetlights in her neighbourhood with energy-saving ones.

p3.en: To get rid of something by putting it in the rubbish; to waste an opportunity.
p3.example: Do not throw e-waste away with general rubbish — take it to a recycling centre.
p3.ex1: She never throws away food if it can be composted or repurposed.
p3.ex2: He was about to throw the old solar panel away before discovering it could be repaired.

p3.en: Units of weight equal to 1,000 kilograms; also used informally to mean a large amount.
p3.example: Millions of tons of plastic waste are produced globally every single year.
p3.ex1: The factory reduced its emissions by hundreds of tons after switching to solar.
p3.ex2: She was shocked to learn how many tons of food are wasted each day.

p3.en: To carry people or goods from one place to another.
p3.example: Locally grown food does not need to be transported long distances, reducing emissions.
p3.ex1: She chooses products that have not been transported across the world.
p3.ex2: Electric vehicles are increasingly used to transport goods in urban areas.

p1.en: An extra item added to something to make it more useful or attractive.
p1.example: She reviewed the latest smartphone accessories on her YouTube channel.
p1.ex1: He bought a new case and other accessories for his phone.
p1.ex2: The unboxing video showed every accessory included in the package.

p1.en: To say that something is true, often something you would prefer not to say.
p1.example: She admitted that she had bought the product just because of the packaging.
p1.ex1: He admitted feeling disappointed when the product did not match the review.
p1.ex2: She admitted spending too much money on gadgets she rarely used.

p1.en: A feeling of excitement about something that is going to happen.
p1.example: The anticipation before an unboxing video is part of its appeal.
p1.ex1: She felt a sense of anticipation as she waited for her order to arrive.
p1.ex2: The channel built anticipation for the new product with teaser videos.

p1.en: A person who competes in sports, especially one who is highly trained.
p1.example: The brand partnered with a famous athlete to promote its new trainers.
p1.ex1: She followed several professional athletes who reviewed sports equipment online.
p1.ex2: The athlete was paid to feature the product in his social media posts.

p1.en: Only just; almost not.
p1.example: The battery barely lasted a day, which was a major disappointment.
p1.ex1: She could barely hear the audio from the new earphones.
p1.ex2: He barely used the app after buying it because it was too complicated.

p1.en: A name or logo that identifies a company or its products.
p1.example: She always buys from the same brand because she trusts its quality.
p1.ex1: The brand launched a new range of eco-friendly products.
p1.ex2: His followers trust his reviews because he is honest about every brand.

p1.en: A YouTube or social media account that publishes content regularly.
p1.example: She runs a popular unboxing channel with over two million subscribers.
p1.ex1: He subscribed to a tech channel that reviews the latest smartphones.
p1.ex2: The channel posted a new video every Friday to keep followers engaged.

p1.en: A person or thing that you spend time with or that accompanies you.
p1.example: A good smartwatch becomes a constant companion throughout the day.
p1.ex1: The app became her daily companion for tracking fitness goals.
p1.ex2: He described his headphones as his most loyal companion at work.

p1.en: Worried or troubled about something.
p1.example: She was concerned about the number of fake reviews on the website.
p1.ex1: He was concerned that the product description was misleading.
p1.ex2: Many consumers are concerned about data privacy when using smart devices.

p1.en: A person who buys goods or uses services.
p1.example: Modern consumers rely heavily on online reviews before making a purchase.
p1.ex1: The brand listened to consumer feedback and improved the product.
p1.ex2: She believed that informed consumers make better purchasing decisions.

p1.en: To separate or detach from a connection; also to stop using technology.
p1.example: She noticed that she felt anxious whenever she disconnected from her phone.
p1.ex1: He decided to disconnect from social media for a week.
p1.ex2: The app disconnected unexpectedly during the live review.

p1.en: Not working correctly; having a defect.
p1.example: She returned the faulty headphones and left a negative review.
p1.ex1: The product turned out to be faulty and stopped working after a week.
p1.ex2: He was frustrated to discover the faulty charger was a safety hazard.

p1.en: An important or interesting quality or part of something.
p1.example: The best feature of the new phone is its incredibly long battery life.
p1.ex1: She listed every feature in her detailed product review.
p1.ex2: The key feature that made her choose that brand was the camera quality.

p1.en: A person who subscribes to or follows someone's social media account.
p1.example: Her unboxing channel gained ten thousand new followers after one viral video.
p1.ex1: He asked his followers to share the review to help more people.
p1.ex2: She built a loyal community of followers who trusted her honest reviews.

p1.en: To work or operate in the correct way.
p1.example: The device failed to function properly after the first software update.
p1.ex1: She checked that all the features functioned as described before writing her review.
p1.ex2: The app functions well on newer devices but struggles on older ones.

p1.en: A message sent by an app or device to inform you of something.
p1.example: She turned off all notifications during the night to improve her sleep.
p1.ex1: He received a notification every time a new review was posted.
p1.ex2: Too many notifications make it hard to focus on important tasks.

p1.en: The act of buying something; also to buy something.
p1.example: She always reads reviews before making an online purchase.
p1.ex1: He regretted his impulse purchase after realising the product was poor quality.
p1.ex2: Consumers are encouraged to purchase locally made products.

p1.en: A suggestion that something is good or suitable for a purpose.
p1.example: She trusted her friend's recommendation over any online review.
p1.ex1: The channel's recommendation led to a huge increase in sales.
p1.ex2: He followed the algorithm's recommendation and discovered a new product brand.

p1.en: Something or someone that takes the place of another.
p1.example: She requested a replacement after the faulty product arrived.
p1.ex1: The company sent a free replacement without asking any questions.
p1.ex2: He was offered a replacement or a full refund for the broken item.

p1.en: To make something known or visible that was previously hidden.
p1.example: The unboxing video slowly reveals each item inside the box.
p1.ex1: She revealed the product in a dramatic way that kept viewers watching.
p1.ex2: The brand chose a big reveal moment to launch the new device.

p1.en: To write or give a critical assessment of a product or service.
p1.example: She reviews new tech products every week on her YouTube channel.
p1.ex1: He reviewed the product honestly, pointing out both its strengths and weaknesses.
p1.ex2: Thousands of customers reviewed the product within days of its release.

p1.en: To follow the progress or movement of something.
p1.example: She uses a fitness app to track her daily steps and calories.
p1.ex1: He tracked his spending on gadgets and was shocked by the total.
p1.ex2: The smartwatch tracks sleep patterns and provides a daily health report.

p1.en: A firm belief in the honesty or reliability of something or someone.
p1.example: Consumer trust in online reviews has decreased due to fake ratings.
p1.ex1: She built trust with her audience by always being honest in her reviews.
p1.ex2: Once a brand loses consumer trust, it is very hard to win it back.

p1.en: A video in which someone opens a product for the first time on camera.
p1.example: Unboxing videos have become one of the most popular formats on YouTube.
p1.ex1: She filmed an unboxing video of the new laptop and got millions of views.
p1.ex2: His unboxing video went viral because the product was completely different from the advertisement.

p1.en: Not certain or confident about something.
p1.example: She was unsure whether to trust the five-star reviews on the website.
p1.ex1: He was unsure which model to choose and watched several reviews.
p1.ex2: She felt unsure about the product after reading mixed feedback from consumers.

p1.en: To remove the wrapping or packaging from something.
p1.example: The excitement of unwrapping a new product is part of the unboxing experience.
p1.ex1: She carefully unwrapped the phone and placed each item on the table.
p1.ex2: Children love to unwrap presents — unboxing videos recreate that feeling.

p1.en: The quality of being useful or practical.
p1.example: She questioned the usefulness of buying a new phone every year.
p1.ex1: The usefulness of the app depended on how often you actually used its features.
p1.ex2: He rated the product based on its usefulness in everyday situations.

p1.en: To consider something important or useful.
p1.example: She values honest reviews more than polished advertisements.
p1.ex1: Consumers value transparency from the brands they support.
p1.ex2: He valued the durability of the product more than its design.

p1.en: A single instance of watching a video; also an opinion.
p1.example: The unboxing video reached ten million views in just three days.
p1.ex1: She shared her view that online reviews are more reliable than advertisements.
p1.ex2: His channel crossed one billion views after the viral product review.

p1.uz: to'liq ma'lumot asosida qaror qabul qilmoq
p1.en: To make choices based on proper knowledge and research.
p1.example: Reading honest reviews helps consumers make informed decisions.
p1.ex1: She always compares products carefully to make informed decisions.
p1.ex2: The goal of the channel is to help viewers make informed decisions when shopping.

p1.ru: В довершение ко всему, ... / Ко всему прочему, ...
p1.en: Used to introduce an additional problem that makes a bad situation even worse.
p1.example: The product arrived late; to make matters worse, it was faulty.
p1.ex1: She lost her charger; to make matters worse, the shop had run out of replacements.
p1.ex2: The review was bad; to make matters worse, the brand responded rudely.

p2.en: The place in a shop where you pay; also the process of paying online.
p2.example: She abandoned her online checkout when she saw the extra delivery charges.
p2.ex1: The queue at the checkout was so long that she left without buying anything.
p2.ex2: He completed the online checkout in less than a minute.

p2.en: An advertisement on television or radio.
p2.example: She skipped the commercial as soon as the skip button appeared.
p2.ex1: The commercial for the new trainers featured a famous athlete.
p2.ex2: He remembered the brand because of a funny commercial he had seen.

p2.en: To make someone believe that something is true or to persuade them to do something.
p2.example: The five-star reviews convinced her to buy the product without hesitation.
p2.ex1: He could not convince his friend that the cheaper brand was just as good.
p2.ex2: The influencer convinced thousands of followers to try the new protein bar.

p2.en: Small files stored on your device by websites to track your online activity.
p2.example: After accepting cookies, she noticed the same products appearing as adverts everywhere.
p2.ex1: He declined the cookies and found that fewer personalised ads appeared.
p2.ex2: Cookies allow websites to remember your preferences and shopping history.

p2.en: Expensive; involving a large amount of money.
p2.example: Replacing a faulty premium product can be extremely costly.
p2.ex1: She decided the costly upgrade was not worth it for such minor improvements.
p2.ex2: He learned that ignoring product reviews can lead to costly mistakes.

p2.en: A large group of people gathered in one place.
p2.example: A crowd gathered around the shop window as the new product was put on display.
p2.ex1: She avoided the shops during peak hours to escape the crowd.
p2.ex2: A crowd of shoppers queued outside the store for the limited edition release.

p2.en: Using resources wisely; not wasteful; offering good value for money.
p2.example: Buying in bulk is often the most economical option for household goods.
p2.ex1: She chose the most economical model that still had all the features she needed.
p2.ex2: He found an economical way to shop by using discount codes and cashback apps.

p2.en: A flat paper container used for sending letters or containing documents.
p2.example: Her online order arrived in a plain brown envelope with no branding.
p2.ex1: She received a coupon in an envelope that gave her ten per cent off.
p2.ex2: He opened the envelope to find a thank-you note from the company.

p2.en: To give something for free, especially as a promotion.
p2.example: The brand gave away free samples at the shopping centre to attract new customers.
p2.ex1: She gave away her old phone when she upgraded to the newer model.
p2.ex2: The company gives away a free accessory with every purchase over fifty pounds.

p2.en: A free gift or competition prize, often used in marketing.
p2.example: She entered the brand's giveaway by tagging three friends in the post.
p2.ex1: The giveaway attracted thousands of new followers to the channel.
p2.ex2: He won a giveaway and received the latest smartphone completely free.

p2.en: To spread rapidly across social media and be seen by a huge number of people.
p2.example: Her unboxing video went viral overnight and gained five million views.
p2.ex1: The honest review went viral because it exposed a popular brand.
p2.ex2: He never expected his simple product video to go viral.

p2.en: Food and other everyday items bought from a supermarket or shop.
p2.example: She switched to online grocery shopping to avoid peak hour crowds.
p2.ex1: He bought his weekly groceries from the local greengrocer and corner shop.
p2.ex2: Ordering groceries online saves time but can be costly if delivery fees are high.

p2.en: A particular way of doing something.
p2.example: Online shopping has become the most popular method of purchasing goods.
p2.ex1: She preferred the old method of trying clothes on before buying.
p2.ex2: His preferred payment method was contactless because it was faster.

p2.en: Arranged to be seen by people, especially in a shop or exhibition.
p2.example: The new products were on display in the shop window to attract customers.
p2.ex1: She stopped to look at the shoes on display in the boutique.
p2.ex2: The limited edition items were on display for only one day.

p2.en: The materials used to wrap or contain a product.
p2.example: She was impressed by the eco-friendly packaging used by the brand.
p2.ex1: The packaging was so attractive that she kept the box after unboxing.
p2.ex2: Poor packaging caused the item to arrive damaged.

p2.en: Advertisements that suddenly appear on a screen while browsing the internet.
p2.example: Pop-up ads interrupted her online shopping experience every few minutes.
p2.ex1: He installed an ad blocker to stop pop-up ads appearing.
p2.ex2: She ignored the pop-up ads but noticed they always showed products she had searched for.

p2.en: A snack bar high in protein, often marketed to fitness enthusiasts.
p2.example: The influencer promoted a protein bar in every video she posted.
p2.ex1: She tried the protein bar after seeing it recommended by a fitness channel.
p2.ex2: He brought protein bars to the gym as a quick post-workout snack.

p2.en: To wait in a line of people for something.
p2.example: Shoppers queued up outside the store hours before it opened for the sale.
p2.ex1: She hated having to queue up at the checkout during the holiday season.
